59: Template style

77: View style
78: ----------
79: 
80: * In Django views, the first parameter in a view function should be called
81:   ``request``.
82: 
83:   Do this::
84: 
85:       def my_view(request, foo):
86:           # ...

88:   Don't do this::
89:

91:           # ...

93: Model style
94: -----------
95: 
96: * Field names should be all lowercase, using underscores instead of
97:   camelCase.
98: 
99:   Do this::
100: 
101:       class Person(models.Model):
102:           first_name = models.CharField(max_length=20)
103:           last_name = models.CharField(max_length=40)
104: 
105:   Don't do this::
106: 
107:       class Person(models.Model):
108:           FirstName = models.CharField(max_length=20)
109:           Last_Name = models.CharField(max_length=40)
110: 
111: * The ``class Meta`` should appear *after* the fields are defined, with
112:   a single blank line separating the fields and the class definition.
113: 
114:   Do this::
115: 
116:       class Person(models.Model):
117:           first_name = models.CharField(max_length=20)
118:           last_name = models.CharField(max_length=40)
119: 
120:           class Meta:
121:               verbose_name_plural = 'people'
122: 
123:   Don't do this::
124: 
125:       class Person(models.Model):
126:           first_name = models.CharField(max_length=20)
127:           last_name = models.CharField(max_length=40)
128:           class Meta:
129:               verbose_name_plural = 'people'
130: 
131:   Don't do this, either::
132: 
133:       class Person(models.Model):
134:           class Meta:
135:               verbose_name_plural = 'people'
136: 
137:           first_name = models.CharField(max_length=20)
138:           last_name = models.CharField(max_length=40)
139: 
140: * If you define a ``__str__`` method (previously ``__unicode__`` before Python 3
141:   was supported), decorate the model class with
142:   :func:`~django.utils.encoding.python_2_unicode_compatible`.
143: 
144: * The order of model inner classes and standard methods should be as
145:   follows (noting that these are not all required):

2: Coding style
3: ============
4: 
5: Please follow these coding standards when writing code for inclusion in Django.
6: 
7: Python style
8: ------------
9: 
10: * Unless otherwise specified, follow :pep:`8`.
11: 
12:   Use `flake8`_ to check for problems in this area. Note that our ``setup.cfg``
13:   file contains some excluded files (deprecated modules we don't care about
14:   cleaning up and some third-party code that Django vendors) as well as some
15:   excluded errors that we don't consider as gross violations. Remember that
16:   :pep:`8` is only a guide, so respect the style of the surrounding code as a
17:   primary goal.
18: 
19:   An exception to :pep:`8` is our rules on line lengths. Don't limit lines of
20:   code to 79 characters if it means the code looks significantly uglier or is
21:   harder to read. We allow up to 119 characters as this is the width of GitHub
22:   code review; anything longer requires horizontal scrolling which makes review
23:   more difficult. This check is included when you run ``flake8``. Documentation,
24:   comments, and docstrings should be wrapped at 79 characters, even though
25:   :pep:`8` suggests 72.
26: 
27: * Use four spaces for indentation.
28: 
29: * Use underscores, not camelCase, for variable, function and method names
30:   (i.e. ``poll.get_unique_voters()``, not ``poll.getUniqueVoters``).
31: 
32: * Use ``InitialCaps`` for class names (or for factory functions that
33:   return classes).
34: 
35: * Use convenience imports whenever available. For example, do this::
36: 
37:       from django.views.generic import View
38: 
39:   Don't do this::
40: 
41:       from django.views.generic.base import View
42: 
43: * In docstrings, use "action words" such as::
44: 
45:       def foo():
46:           """
47:           Calculates something and returns the result.
48:           """

153:   * Any custom methods

155: * If ``choices`` is defined for a given model field, define each choice as
156:   a tuple of tuples, with an all-uppercase name as a class attribute on the
157:   model. Example::
158: 
159:     class MyModel(models.Model):
160:         DIRECTION_UP = 'U'
161:         DIRECTION_DOWN = 'D'
162:         DIRECTION_CHOICES = (
163:             (DIRECTION_UP, 'Up'),
164:             (DIRECTION_DOWN, 'Down'),
165:         )
166: 
167: Use of ``django.conf.settings``
168: -------------------------------
169: 
170: Modules should not in general use settings stored in ``django.conf.settings``
171: at the top level (i.e. evaluated when the module is imported). The explanation
172: for this is as follows:
173: 
174: Manual configuration of settings (i.e. not relying on the
175: ``DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE`` environment variable) is allowed and possible as
176: follows::
177: 
178:     from django.conf import settings
179: 
180:     settings.configure({}, SOME_SETTING='foo')
181: 
182: However, if any setting is accessed before the ``settings.configure`` line,
183: this will not work. (Internally, ``settings`` is a ``LazyObject`` which
184: configures itself automatically when the settings are accessed if it has not
185: already been configured).
186: 
187: So, if there is a module containing some code as follows::
188: 
189:     from django.conf import settings
190:     from django.core.urlresolvers import get_callable
191: 
192:     default_foo_view = get_callable(settings.FOO_VIEW)
193: 
194: ...then importing this module will cause the settings object to be configured.
195: That means that the ability for third parties to import the module at the top
196: level is incompatible with the ability to configure the settings object
197: manually, or makes it very difficult in some circumstances.
198: 
199: Instead of the above code, a level of laziness or indirection must be used,
200: such as ``django.utils.functional.LazyObject``,
201: ``django.utils.functional.lazy()`` or ``lambda``.
202: 
203: Miscellaneous
204: -------------
205: 
206: * Mark all strings for internationalization; see the :doc:`i18n
207:   documentation </topics/i18n/index>` for details.
208: 
209: * Remove ``import`` statements that are no longer used when you change code.
210:   `flake8`_ will identify these imports for you. If an unused import needs to
211:   remain for backwards-compatibility, mark the end of with ``# NOQA`` to
212:   silence the flake8 warning.
213: 
214: * Systematically remove all trailing whitespaces from your code as those
215:   add unnecessary bytes, add visual clutter to the patches and can also
216:   occasionally cause unnecessary merge conflicts. Some IDE's can be
217:   configured to automatically remove them and most VCS tools can be set to
218:   highlight them in diff outputs.
219: 
220: * Please don't put your name in the code you contribute. Our policy is to
221:   keep contributors' names in the ``AUTHORS`` file distributed with Django
222:   -- not scattered throughout the codebase itself. Feel free to include a
223:   change to the ``AUTHORS`` file in your patch if you make more than a
224:   single trivial change.
225: 
226: .. _flake8: https://pypi.python.org/pypi/flake8"}
